name: Eagle
tagline: Desktop app for organizing, tagging and searching large libraries of images, design files and other visual assets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Eagle is sold as a one-time license rather than a subscription.

verdictSummary: Eagle is a local app with no network, no cloud account and no data moat, so nothing structural stops you from building your own. An agent can produce a working tag-and-search library over a folder of images in a sitting, and it will feel great at 500 files. The pain starts at 50,000 files, mixed formats and long sessions: thumbnail pipelines, virtualized grids that do not stutter, PSD and AI and Sketch previews, font and video handling, duplicate detection, color search, and a browser extension that saves images with their source URL. That is all shippable, just not in one sitting, and the polish gap stays visible for a long time. Worth noting the thing you are replacing is a one-time purchase, which makes the build-versus-buy math less flattering than usual.
coreLoopDIY: Indexes a local folder tree of images, generates thumbnails, and gives you a fast virtualized grid with folders, tags, ratings, color filter and full-text search over notes and filenames.
requirements: sharp (libvips) for thumbnails and color extraction
SQLite file for the index, images stay on disk
Optional: ffmpeg on PATH if you want video thumbnails
whatYouLose: Preview and thumbnail support for design formats: PSD, AI, Sketch, Figma exports, fonts, 3D files
The browser extension that captures images with source URL, dimensions and page context in one click
Drag-out-to-any-app behavior that makes it usable as a real asset shelf rather than a viewer
Smart folders, duplicate detection, similar-image search and color-similarity search tuned to actually work
Performance that holds at six-figure library sizes with instant scroll and instant filter
moatNotes: The moat is entirely craft: fast thumbnails, jank-free scrolling at scale, and the long tail of file formats nobody wants to write parsers for.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because it is a one-time license for software that has already solved the boring half of the problem. The value of an asset manager is measured in how little you think about it while scrolling 80,000 files, and that is exactly the part a weekend build gets wrong. Once a library is tagged, annotated and structured inside Eagle, moving out means re-deriving all of that metadata, which is a mild but real switching cost. A DIY version is a genuinely good project if your library is small, your formats are boring, or you want indexing rules Eagle refuses to give you.
notes: Rare case where the honest answer is that the build is fun but the license is cheap.
prompt:
Build a local-first visual asset manager that runs on my own machine. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 20 + Express backend, TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for the index (file at ./data/library.db)
- sharp for thumbnails and dominant-color extraction
- React + Vite + Tailwind frontend, react-window for grid virtualization
- Single `npm run dev` starts API on 3001 and UI on 5173 with a proxy

Core behavior:
- I point it at one or more root folders via a LIBRARY_ROOTS value in .env (comma separated)
- On start it walks those roots, indexes jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/avif/svg/bmp/tiff, and stores path, filename, size, dimensions, mtime, sha1
- Never move, rename or modify source files. Images stay exactly where they are on disk
- Generate 400px webp thumbnails into ./data/thumbs keyed by sha1, skip if already present
- Extract 5 dominant colors per image with sharp and store them as hex
- Rescan on demand via a button, plus a chokidar watcher for adds and deletes

UI, single page:
- Left sidebar: folder tree from the indexed roots, tag list with counts, rating filter, color swatch filter
- Main area: virtualized square-thumbnail grid, adjustable thumbnail size slider, lazy-loaded thumbs
- Click opens a detail panel: full-size preview, metadata, editable tags, 0-5 rating, free-text note
- Top bar: search box doing SQLite FTS5 over filename, tags and notes, with instant results
- Multi-select with shift and cmd click, bulk add or remove tags on the selection
- Keyboard: arrows to move, space to preview, t to focus tag input, delete does nothing destructive

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- PSD, AI, Sketch, font or 3D previews
- Browser extension, drag-out to other apps, sync, sharing, mobile

Deliver a README with setup steps, an .env.example with LIBRARY_ROOTS, and seed nothing. It must run on a folder of 20,000 images without the grid stuttering: do the work in the indexer, not the render path.
